column2: On the authority of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Allah the Exalted said: O son of Ādam,
as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for whatever you have done, and I do not mind. O son of Ādam,
if your sins were to reach the clouds of the sky and you then sought My forgiveness, I would forgive you. O son of Ādam,

if you were to come to Me with sins nearly filling the earth, and then meet Me without associating anything with Me, I would come to you with forgiveness nearly filling it.” Reported by al-Tirmidhī, who said: “An authentic hadith.”
This hadith is the last of the hadiths that al-Nawawī (may Allah have mercy on him) included in his book the Forty, which contains two hadiths more than forty,

so calling it “the Forty” is a matter of using the round number and dropping the extra units. This hadith is a ḥadīth qudsī, one of those the Messenger of Allah ﷺ relates from his Lord, Blessed and Exalted is He.

The address in the hadith is to the children of Ādam. It shows that among the causes of the forgiveness of sins are calling upon Allah and hoping for the forgiveness of sins from Him, seeking His forgiveness for them, sincerity to Allah and freedom from shirk. The meaning of the forgiveness of sins is concealing them from creation and overlooking them, so that one is not punished for them.
His words, “O son of Ādam,

as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for whatever you have done, and I do not mind”: the servant's calling upon his Lord to forgive his sins, and his hoping for that from Him without despair, together with repentance from sins, brings about forgiveness from Allah, however great, many and repeated the sins may be.

That is why He said: “for whatever you have done, and I do not mind.” Similar to this are the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: “Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful” [al-Zumar 39:53].
His words, “O son of Ādam,

if your sins were to reach the clouds of the sky (ʿanān al-samāʾ) and you then sought My forgiveness, I would forgive you”: if the servant's sins became so many that they reached ʿanān al-samāʾ, that is,
reached the sky, or something below that such as the clouds, or as far as the eye can see looking upwards, and then the servant sought forgiveness, together with repentance from all his sins,
Allah the Exalted would forgive those sins and overlook them. Repentance consists of giving up the sin, regretting what is past, and resolving for the future not to return to it.

Along with these three, if the sin was against the right of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and has an expiation, he performs the expiation; and if it concerns the rights of human beings, he restores their rights to them or seeks their release from them.
His words, “O son of Ādam,

if you were to come to Me with sins nearly filling the earth, and then meet Me without associating anything with Me, I would come to you with forgiveness nearly filling it”: associating partners with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the sin that Allah does not forgive.

Every sin less than shirk is subject to the will of Allah: if He wills, He pardons its doer and does not punish him; and if He wills, He punishes him and admits him to the Fire, but he will not abide in it forever as the disbelievers do;

rather, he will inevitably come out of it and enter Paradise, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: “Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills” [al-Nisāʾ 4:48],

in two verses of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. This hadith makes clear that, however many sins there may be, Allah overlooks them, on condition that the servant makes his worship sincerely for Allah and is free of associating partners with Him.
The favour of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is vast, and He forgives His servants' sins.
Among the causes of the forgiveness of sins are calling upon Allah and hoping in Him without despair.
The hadith shows the merit of seeking forgiveness together with repentance: Allah forgives the sins of the one who seeks forgiveness, however many they may be.
Associating partners with Allah is the sin that is not forgiven, and everything besides it is subject to the will of Allah.
The hadith shows the merit of sincerity: Allah expiates sins by it.
